scenario.name: Microsoft WER, Mandiant & Elastic DFIR — IFEO SilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe LSASS Dump Hijack (Sysmon EID 12 / 13)
scenario.overview: Picture a grand central train station with an arched iron canopy, hanging station clock, ticket turnstiles, parallel railway tracks, and a sleek express train waiting at the platform. Beneath the central train station canopy, a stowaway slips past the platform ticket barrier using a copied conductor punch card right before boarding time. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the platform ticket barrier in tiny disguised batches, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the station conductor's station. The station master’s glowing track-indicator board flashes a route mismatch the instant the express train leaves its scheduled platform line. In this scenario (T1546.012, Microsoft WER, Mandiant & Elastic DFIR, IFEO SilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe LSASS Dump Hijack (Sysmon EID 12 / 13)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: enabling IFEO (FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT), then configuring SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe (LAUNCH_NOTIFYPROCESS | LOCAL_DUMP), then triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit (Source: Winlogon / SilentProcessExit). Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Enabling IFEO (FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT), then Configuring SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe (LAUNCH_NOTIFYPROCESS | LOCAL_DUMP), then Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit (Source: Winlogon / SilentProcessExit). Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 13 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 3: Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump (Application EventID 3001)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1003.001 - Trusted WerFault.exe Proxy Dumping LSASS)
stages.description: With the station clock ticking, the express locomotive pulls onto the alternate siding where unauthorized cargo bags are transferred off the rear coach. In this final step inside the train station, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the station conductor's station until the station master signal board catches the mismatch. The attacker calls ntdll.dll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit(hLsass, 0) (which only requires PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ or is triggered via CreateRemoteThread/NtTerminateProcess on a helper). The Windows Error Reporting service spawns the Microsoft-signed C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe, which dumps lsass.exe-(PID).dmp into C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps, spawns MonitorProcess, and logs Application EventID 3001 (Source: Winlogon / SilentProcessExit) (logged in Sysmon Event 10 with EventID=10 , ProcessAccess + 11 , FileCreate + 3001 , Application Log, ProxyBinary=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe , Microsoft Signed, TargetProcess=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe, CreatedDumpFile=C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps\lsass.exe-684.dmp so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ntdll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit(hProcess, 0) -> LPC message to WerSvcGroup (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ntdll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit, hProcess, 0 -> LPC message to WerSvcGroup via System / Run so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump , Application EventID 3001" , The attacker calls ntdll while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 10: SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe GrantedAccess=0x1FFFFF runs (which invokes or targets the host daemon/process , Sysmon EventID 10: SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass. so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump , Application EventID 3001" , The attacker calls ntdll while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe -u -p 684 -s 1420 (Dumping lsass.exe via SilentProcessExit) / ⇠#3 ACK 10) from Node ③ (#3 IFEO GlobalFlag (0x200)) to Node ④ (#4 SilentProcessExit\lsass.exe), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 WerFault.exe (Trusted Dumper)).

steps.plainTitle: Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump (Application EventID 3001)
steps.storyAnalogy: With the station clock ticking, the express locomotive pulls onto the alternate siding where unauthorized cargo bags are transferred off the rear coach. In this final step inside the train station, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the station conductor's station until the station master signal board catches the mismatch.
steps.simpleExplanation: The attacker calls ntdll.dll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit(hLsass, 0) (which only requires PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ or is triggered via CreateRemoteThread/NtTerminateProcess on a helper). The Windows Error Reporting service spawns the Microsoft-signed C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe, which dumps lsass.exe-(PID).dmp into C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps, spawns MonitorProcess, and logs Application EventID 3001 (Source: Winlogon / SilentProcessExit) (logged in Sysmon Event 10 with EventID=10 , ProcessAccess + 11 , FileCreate + 3001 , Application Log, ProxyBinary=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe , Microsoft Signed, TargetProcess=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe, CreatedDumpFile=C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps\lsass.exe-684.dmp so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes ntdll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit(hProcess, 0) -> LPC message to WerSvcGroup (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ntdll!RtlReportSilentProcessExit, hProcess, 0 -> LPC message to WerSvcGroup via System / Run so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump , Application EventID 3001" , The attacker calls ntdll while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 10: SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe GrantedAccess=0x1FFFFF runs (which invokes or targets the host daemon/process , Sysmon EventID 10: SourceImage=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe TargetImage=C:\Windows\System32\lsass. so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1003.001 during "Triggering RtlReportSilentProcessExit & WerFault.exe Full LSASS Dump , Application EventID 3001" , The attacker calls ntdll while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).

steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 10 (recording EventID=10 , ProcessAccess + 11 , FileCreate + 3001 , Application Log, ProxyBinary=C:\Windows\System32\WerFault.exe , Microsoft Signed, TargetProcess=C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe, CreatedDumpFile=C:\Windows\Temp\Dumps\lsass.exe-684.dmp under T1003.001): Do not blindly exclude WerFault.exe or wermgr.exe from Sysmon EventID 10 (TargetImage=lsass.exe) or EventID 11 (*.dmp creation); correlate WerFault.exe LSASS access against SilentProcessExit registry keys.
